__comment: EduRankAI Mail — stack dashboard. Edited as a file, not in the UI (allowUiUpdates is false). TWO NAMESPACES: edurankai_mail_* comes from the application (/api/metrics, src/lib/mailplatform) and its COUNTERS are process-local on serverless — read edurankai_mail_registry_age_seconds before drawing conclusions from a low counter. era_* comes from this stack's own long-lived services on the ZBook, where counters behave normally. Panel order is deliberate: the top row answers 'is it broken', everything below is evidence.
title: EduRankAI Mail — stack

panels.title: Components up
panels.description: era_mailops_component_up per component, from the stack's health aggregator. A component that is NOT deployed emits no series at all rather than a zero — so an empty tile means 'nothing is running', not 'everything is fine'.

panels.title: Telemetry trustworthy?
panels.description: edurankai_mail_telemetry_readable is 0 when the app could not read queue telemetry from Postgres — every queue_* number in this dashboard is then a DEFAULT, not a measurement. Read this tile before believing the queue panels. A quiet queue and an unreadable one must never look alike.

panels.title: Registry age
panels.description: edurankai_mail_registry_age_seconds — seconds since the serving instance created its metric registry. Application COUNTERS are only meaningful relative to this. A young registry after a deploy makes real traffic look like a collapse; this tile is how you tell the two apart.

panels.title: Queue depth by status
panels.description: edurankai_mail_queue_depth — read from Postgres at scrape time, so unlike the counters this IS a cluster-wide view. pending+processing is the backlog and is the number that must not grow without bound. `failed` is the parked pile: those jobs will not run again without /api/jobs/run?action=retry.

panels.title: Oldest job age
panels.description: edurankai_mail_queue_oldest_age_seconds. Depth can look healthy while the HEAD of the queue is stuck — a few jobs nothing will claim. This is the panel that catches that. The series is ABSENT when the queue is empty, deliberately: absent and zero mean different things, and a zero would read as 'the head is fresh'.

panels.title: Worker activity (ZBook)
panels.description: era_worker_consecutive_errors above zero means the worker cannot reach the app or its CRON_SECRET is wrong — queued mail is not lost, but nothing is being sent. A stopped worker and an overloaded one look identical from backlog alone, so read this panel before concluding it is a capacity problem.

panels.title: Inbound bridge (ZBook)
panels.description: received vs forwarded vs refused. A gap between received and forwarded means messages are being held and retried. `refused` means the app answered 4xx — the message is not lost (the bridge answers 451, so the upstream MTA keeps it) but it is not being delivered either. Almost always a secret mismatch.

panels.title: Message outcomes (application)
panels.description: PROCESS-LOCAL counters. On serverless each instance keeps its own registry and is recycled without warning, so a scrape sees one instance since its cold start — check the Registry age tile before reading a drop as a traffic collapse. A sustained RATIO between these series is meaningful; an absolute rate is not a cluster total.

panels.title: Probe latency (ZBook)
panels.description: Round-trip of each health probe from the aggregator. A component going slow before it goes down is the earliest warning this stack produces; watch for a step change rather than an absolute value.

panels.title: Captured test mail (sink)
panels.description: era_sink_messages — messages the sink has captured since it started. The sink DELIVERS NOTHING; it exists so load and integration tests can never reach a real recipient. A rising line during a load test is the test working.
